topic: Modern C++ Template Programming with Type Deduction and SFINAE
explanation: In modern C++, template programming allows writing generic, type-independent code that can operate on various data types. Type deduction, enabled by keywords like auto and decltype, simplifies code by automatically inferring types. SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) is a compile-time technique used to enable or disable template instantiations based on type traits, facilitating advanced template specialization and conditional compilation. Together, these features enable highly flexible, efficient, and type-safe generic programming aligned with modern C++ idioms.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates modern C++ template programming by defining a function template 'is_even' that uses type deduction to accept any type. The use of std::enable_if combined with std::is_integral ensures that 'is_even' is only instantiated for integral types, leveraging SFINAE to conditionally enable the function. The main function calls 'is_even' with an integer, which compiles successfully, illustrating how templates and type traits enable type-safe, generic programming in C++.
